name: PT Chandra Daya Investasi TBK.

frontmatter.title: Chandra Daya Investasi: the operating business grew, the reported profit did not
frontmatter.summary: Nine-month profit fell because last year's one-off other gain did not repeat and finance costs rose; fair-value income was flat. Management's EBITDA growth is largely non-operating. We refresh the price to the 29 October close, put the EV/EBITDA cross-check on the filing's EBITDA, restore the house method weights and remove an unsourced loan haircut. The refinancing wall and the unfunded AMP subscription are now in the risks; target Rp287 and rating REDUCE.
thesis: Four infrastructure pillars inside the Chandra Asri group: electricity distribution in the Krakatau industrial estate, water, tank and jetty storage, and marine and land logistics [S4, S5].

The nine-month result splits the story: time charter revenue reached US$40.0m, already above the US$34.6m earned in the whole of FY2025, while electricity and tank rental fell; the growth is real but concentrated in the lowest-visibility pillar [S17, S4].

Reported profit fell 61.5% because the prior year's one-off other gain of US$45.4m did not repeat - this year's line was US$3.5m - and finance costs rose to US$40.2m, while fair-value income was flat at US$16.8m and the operating business grew [S17].

A large related-party financial portfolio - equity-linked bonds issued by the parent, quoted shares and a loan receivable from CAP subsidiaries - sits alongside the operating assets and must be valued separately [S4, S17].

Leverage is the binding constraint: nine-month finance costs exceed the operating result, operating cash flow is negative, and debt of US$894.3m carries US$272.2m of principal due in 2031 and US$166.7m in 2032, with US$90.0m of AMP subscription still to fund [S17, S2].

The shares trade at 3.0x our fundamental value; the premium is a float and regime variable, not an earnings variable, and the March 2027 free-float step is the dated force that should compress part of it [S10, S8].

catalysts.event: First free-float deadline for large caps below the intermediate threshold [S8]
End of the MSCI consultation feedback period on Standalone status for Indonesia [S11]
MSCI decision on the Standalone proposal [S11]
Target commercial operation of the port and storage projects funded from the IPO proceeds [S14]

blocks.text: What changed. The price is refreshed to the 29 October close of Rp362, not the intraday datapack print carried last time [S0]. The EV/EBITDA cross-check now uses the filing's EBITDA instead of the data pack's depreciation error, the house method weights are restored, the related-party loan is carried at face rather than an unsourced haircut, and the refinancing calendar and unfunded AMP subscription are now risks [S0, S17, S2]. The target is Rp287 and the rating REDUCE.

The event. Revenue rose to US$122.0m from US$104.8m, up 16.0%, while net profit fell to US$32.2m from US$83.5m, down 61.5% [S17, S14]. The decline is neither the operating business nor a fair-value non-repeat: financial-asset income was US$16.8m, flat on the prior year, and the swing is the one-off other gain, US$45.4m a year earlier against US$3.5m now, plus finance costs of US$40.2m [S17].

The EBITDA headline needs care. Management reports US$49.9m, up 65.0%, a 41.0% margin [S14]; on our definition - gross profit less selling and administrative costs plus depreciation - the margin is about half, because the figure is lifted by associate income of US$10.5m, the foreign-exchange gain of US$12.9m and fair-value income of US$16.8m [S17].

We recalibrated three inputs. The nine-month post-depreciation gross margin fell as depreciation stepped up faster than the ex-depreciation margin [S17, F55, F56], so we model 22.0% for FY2026E. Capex ran at US$121.3m in nine months but the quarterly pace halved, so we model 85.0% of revenue rather than one times [S17, S9]. Debt ended at US$894.3m against US$485.9m of cash, and we carry the actual increase as net borrowing [S17].

Fundamental value is Rp130 against Rp362 [S2]. The konglo lens keeps part of the gap: the price is 3.0x today's value of Rp120, the base regime case closes 35.0% of the log gap, and the target of Rp287 is a return of -20.5% [S2, S10]. The premium rests on a 9.8% float against a 12.5% threshold due in March 2027 and on a controller holding 60.0% [S10, S8]. Three things move the value: capex normalisation, an electricity recovery, and the float repair [S17, S9, S8].

CDIA reports four segments: energy, logistics, tank and jetty rental, and other services [S17]. Electricity and other electrical services earned US$67.1m, time charter services US$40.0m, fuel sales US$8.3m, tank and jetty rental US$3.7m, warehouse rental US$1.5m and other services the balance [S17]. Energy is still close to two thirds of revenue but fell year on year, while time charter rose to US$40.0m in nine months against US$34.6m for all of FY2025 [S17].

Energy earned US$12.2m of segment result and logistics US$10.4m in the nine months, so the smaller half of revenue now earns nearly as much as the larger half [S17]. That is the case for the logistics build-out and its vulnerability: charter rates are the one input the group does not control [S4]. The group also subscribed for US$90.0m of new shares in PT Armada Maritim Persada, a shipping associate that adds mining-logistics and port-management exposure [S17, S13].

The energy pillar runs a gas and steam combined-cycle plant of 120 MW serving the Krakatau industrial estate and about 311 electricity customers, and holds an interest in an associate operating a 200 MW coal-fired plant [S5]; it commissioned a bitumen tank at Merak in October 2026 [S6]. Management says more than nine tenths of revenue is contract-based, but the filing's related-party share is 23.2% of nine-month revenue, up from 17.2%, with CAP at US$12.8m the only customer above a tenth [S14, S17]. CAP holds 60.0%, Phoenix Power B.V. 30.0%, the public 10.0%, and the company 79.5m treasury shares [S2, S17]. Phoenix sits in the EGCO chain, so control runs through CAP [S5, S4].

In electricity CDIA is the incumbent distributor inside the Krakatau industrial estate, buying bulk power and gas and reselling to tenants under long-term arrangements; in logistics and storage it is a challenger in a fragmented market [S5, S9]. The moat is the estate - duplicating substations, water treatment and jetty access makes little sense, and the customer relationships are long-dated - and it does not extend into shipping, where charter rates are set competitively [S5]. Buyer power is high in electricity, supplier power is high because the state utility supplies the bulk power, and entry barriers are the concession and the capital for tanks and vessels [S4].

The regulation that matters most is capital-markets regulation. The exchange has raised the minimum free float and set staged deadlines: large caps below the intermediate threshold must reach it by the end of March 2027 and the full minimum a year later [S8], and OJK has retained an exit-policy option [S7]. MSCI's consultation on moving Indonesia to Standalone status, with a decision due by June 2027, is the second dated regime event [S11].

The group buys scale rather than builds it, which makes acquisition price and fleet utilisation the swing factors in returns; the vessel allocation from the IPO is fully deployed, while the port and storage segment targets commercial operation in 2027 [S4, S5, S14].

Revenue rose to US$122.0m in the nine months from US$104.8m, leaving gross profit of US$25.6m against US$24.0m [S17]. All the growth came from logistics: time charter revenue was US$40.0m, while electricity slipped to US$67.1m and tank and jetty rental to US$3.7m [S17, S4].

Our EBITDA history is rebuilt from the filing: depreciation was US$14.9m in the nine months alone, against US$9.6m in FY2025 and US$8.6m in FY2024 [S17, S4]. On that basis the nine-month operating EBITDA is about half of management's US$49.9m, and the gap is associate income of US$10.5m, the foreign-exchange gain of US$12.9m and fair-value income of US$16.8m [S17].

The profit line carries the quality question. Profit before tax was US$44.5m against US$12.4m of tax, leaving US$32.2m, of which US$30.3m went to shareholders [S17]. Below the operating line sat finance income of US$29.9m, fair-value income of US$16.8m, associate income of US$10.5m, a foreign-exchange gain of US$12.9m and other gains of US$3.5m, against finance costs of US$40.2m [S17]. The prior-year other-gains line was US$45.4m and financial-asset income was the same US$16.8m: the decline is the non-recurring gain plus higher finance costs, not a missing mark [S17, S14].

The AMP subscription is the new cash commitment. A subsidiary agreed on 30 June 2026 to subscribe new shares representing 40.0% of PT Armada Maritim Persada for US$90.0m; US$30.0m was paid and US$31.0m is carried as an associate [S17]. The balance is unfunded: it converts into an asset at cost, so it is not a claim in the bridge, but it is a cash call on a group with negative operating cash flow, funded from the same bank lines as the capex [S17, S13].

Net cash used in operating activities was US$6.3m, against US$7.7m provided a year earlier, while capex was US$121.3m and the related-party loan absorbed US$235.0m [S17]. The group funded that with US$50.0m of dividends, a US$4.6m buyback and new long-term bank loans, lifting debt to US$894.3m from US$562.6m; cash rose to US$485.9m [S17].

The balance sheet carries US$2,066.0m of assets and US$954.5m of liabilities, the latter almost entirely bank debt [S17]. Alongside the business sits a financial portfolio: US$358.1m of bonds, US$230.3m of quoted shares, a US$245.2m loan from CAP subsidiaries and US$205.1m of associates [S17]. The portfolio and the loan exceed gross debt.

Earnings-quality flags. The fair-value line is a mark, not cash; related-party revenue is 23.2% of the total, up from 17.2%; and the largest financial asset is a bond issued by the controlling shareholder's listed vehicle [S17, S4]. Management's EBITDA is not reconciled to operating profit [S14, S17]. Those are optics-class, not manipulation-class: everything is disclosed, and quality depends on the parent's credit. On accruals, net profit of US$32.2m against an operating cash outflow of US$6.3m on average assets of US$2,066.0m (US$1,743.8m at the prior year-end) is a low single-digit ratio, well inside the card's alarm level [S17]. The trend is the signal: operating cash covered under a tenth of profit a year earlier and is negative now.

Our forecast holds the last actual's economics on a corrected base. Revenue grows 16.0% in FY2026E, fading to 8.0% [S17]. The post-depreciation gross margin is 22.0%, rising to the FY2025 level as the fleet annualises; operating costs are about 10.0% of revenue and depreciation 11.5% [S17, S4]. Capex is 85.0% of revenue, fading to a steady reinvestment rate above depreciation [S17, S9]. Operating EBIT is taxed at 22.0%; net borrowing of US$331.7m reflects the actual nine-month increase [S17].

On those inputs FY2026E revenue is US$171.7m and EBITDA US$40.4m, a margin of 23.5%, with net profit of US$25.3m [S2]. The model's net debt/EBITDA of 6.4x flatters the position because its cash line does not deduct the portfolio the bridge carries as an asset, so the 30 September filing is the one to use for leverage [S2, S17]. On the house AFFO definition - EBITDA less depreciation, cash interest and cash tax - the result is negative, and the positive FCFE yield of 9.1% is manufactured by net borrowing [S2, S4].

We value CDIA on the house power-utilities method set at the house weights: the DCF carries 60%, the EV/EBITDA cross-check 30% and the dividend-yield check 10%; the P/E check is dropped because it would capitalise the FY2025 fair-value gain and FVTPL marks in parent earnings [S4, S17]. The methods fit because the estate, tank and jetty contracts are long-dated and capital-intensive and reported multiples are distorted by non-operating income [S4, S17]. The DCF is primary at Rp92 a share.

The cost of capital is a house build, not a company disclosure: a rupiah risk-free rate of 5.0%, a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2%, a country risk premium of 2.5% and the house unlevered beta for power utilities of 0.60, levered to 0.74, giving a cost of equity of 10.0% and a WACC of 8.9%; the cost of debt of 7.0% is checked against the filing's loan pricing [S4, S2]. The registry's one-year beta is 1.99 [S10], but it measures a year in which the shares fell by four fifths, not operating risk; at that beta the WACC would leave the sensitivity grid. Gearing uses the market capitalisation at the 29 October close, itself 3.0x fundamental value, so WACC is understated against a fundamental capital structure - a bias that flatters the DCF [S0].

The DCF gives an enterprise value of US$77.1m for the operating business, with 166.8% of it in the terminal period, because the explicit years are cash-negative [S2, S17]. Adding the financial portfolio, the associates at book, the related-party loan at face and the quoted shares at fair value, and deducting net debt and minorities, gives the value; the bridge stays at the 30 June balance sheet, and third-quarter movements net to under one per cent of bridge equity [S2, S17].

Three holdings need the recovery test. The related-party loan is US$245.2m, three loans to CAP subsidiaries at a 12.0% fixed coupon maturing 2030-2035, with no impairment provision disclosed; we carry it at face, the same basis as the filing [S2, F24]. The US$358.1m equity-linked bond holding is marked at fair value and carries a 51.0% option over CAP's terminal and storage subsidiary; the option sits inside the mark [S2]. The associates of US$205.1m include KPE at US$79.3m [S2]. The annual report's "worth" line of US$200.0m describes the KPE stake at acquisition, not a carrying value; book reflects equity after project debt, and the 2023 top-up of the remaining stake cost US$46.4m, consistent with a lower equity value than the enterprise worth [S5, S2]. KPE contributed US$2.4m of associate profit in the first half with no impairment indicator, so book is the most likely mark [S2]. The port and storage projects are inside the forecast cash flows and target operation in 2027 [S14].

The EV/EBITDA cross-check now tests the DCF instead of the data pack's error. It applies the peer median of 15.9x to the last audited EBITDA rebuilt from the filing, giving Rp155, 67.5% above the DCF [S0, S4, F56]. The four names with an EV/EBITDA are BREN, KEEN, PGEO and POWR; the median is set by the two middle names, and BREN is highest because it is a Barito sibling carrying its own konglo premium [S0]. The divergence describes the sector's rating, not CDIA's cash flow, so the DCF stays primary [S2]. The dividend-yield check adds Rp138 on a peer median yield of 1.0%, but our forecast dividend is a token distribution on depressed earnings, so it is the weakest check [S2, S17].

The konglo lens sets most of the target. The price is 3.0x our fundamental value today of Rp120, and the lens keeps a probability-weighted share of the premium over three regime scenarios: the base case closes 35.0% of the log gap, the bear 75.0% and the bull -10.0% [S2]. The closing share is raised by the free-float deadline: the registry float is 9.8% against a next step of 12.5% in March 2027, 5.0 months away [S10, S8]. The target is Rp287; the base regime scenario alone is Rp267, the bear Rp172 and the bull Rp440 [S2]. The target sits far above fundamental value: a thin float can keep a premium alive longer than a gap can close. The reverse DCF implies revenue growth of 25.8%, a pace not sustained outside the acquisition year [S9, S17].

The heaviest risk is ownership. The registry float is 9.8% against a minimum that rises in stages, with the first deadline on 31 March 2027 [S10, S8, S7]. The step to 12.5% is 2.7% of the register, several billion shares at Rp362 - weeks of average daily turnover - while a failure to sell down invites the exit-policy discussion [S7, S10]. A placement or rights issue is the alternative remedy; we model no issuance because none has been announced [S8, S10].

Leverage and refinancing are now a named risk. Finance costs of US$40.2m in nine months are more than triple the operating result, and even FY2025 finance costs of US$28.9m exceeded operating profit of US$22.3m [S17, S4]. Operating cash flow was an outflow of US$6.3m against an inflow of US$7.7m a year earlier, and the dividend of US$50.0m and the buyback of US$4.6m were funded with new bank debt, taking debt to US$894.3m [S17]. The calendar is not near-term: US$272.2m falls due in 2031, US$166.7m in 2032 and US$103.0m in 2035, against US$772.6m of total principal; the Rp4tn term loan maturing in 2031 carries a debt-to-equity covenant of 3.0 times, and debt is a fraction of equity, so the covenant is not the constraint - liquidity is [S2, S17]. The AMP balance and negative operating cash flow are funded from the same bank lines; if lending tightens, the remedies are portfolio asset sales or a rights issue [S17]. A rights issue at today's premium would lift fundamental value per share but compress the konglo premium: the dilution risk sits on the premium, not the DCF. The bear case does not model a covenant breach because the headroom does not support one; the funding path is what turns it into a sell-down story [S2, S17].

The related-party exposure is the largest single balance-sheet risk, and it grew: the loan to CAP subsidiaries is US$245.2m against nil a year earlier, the parent-issued equity-linked bonds are US$358.1m, and related-party revenue rose to 23.2% [S17, S4]. These are disclosed and marked, so optics-class; but quality depends on the parent's credit [S17].

Operationally, electricity revenue fell while tank and jetty rental slipped; growth is carried by time charter, the segment with the least contract visibility [S17]. The AMP subscription adds mining-logistics and port exposure but also a cash commitment ahead of any contribution [S13, S17].

The bull case is a re-rating, not a float fix. A placement or controller sell-down increases supply and should compress the premium, so the bull regime target of Rp440 is not built on it. The channel that widens the premium is index flows: MSCI keeps Indonesia in the Emerging index at the June 2027 decision and lifts its freeze, so passive money returns to a float of 9.8% once the company meets the March steps; an accretive asset injection at a fair price is the second channel [S11, S8, S5]. Float repair compresses; index re-inclusion re-rates, and the re-rating lives in the bull [S2].

The business scenarios - bear, base and bull with probabilities of 25%, 50% and 25% - drive fundamental value: the bear takes it to Rp109 and the bull to Rp159 [S2]. The bear assumes softer charter rates and margin compression with the funding path under stress; the bull assumes faster integration and earlier capex normalisation [S17, S4]. The konglo lens is the second, separate layer, driven by the free-float deadline inside the window [S2, S8].

Signposts that would change the view: a controller sell-down or placement that lifts the float; the March 2027 review; the MSCI decision; a material related-party transaction; a refinancing at a higher spread; and a stabilisation in electricity and tank revenue [S8, S2, S17].

CDIA is a Prajogo Pangestu family-controlled company, a subsidiary of Chandra Asri Pacific within the Barito group. CAP holds 60.0%, Phoenix Power B.V. 30.0%, the public 10.0% and the company 79.5m treasury shares [S2, S17]. Phoenix sits in the EGCO Group chain, not the family block, so control runs through CAP [S5, S4]. The registry float is 9.8%, below the audited public block, which keeps the market price float-driven and is why the konglo lens rather than the DCF sets the target [S10, S4].

The free-float rule is the governance event of the next eighteen months: large caps below the intermediate threshold must reach it by 31 March 2027, OJK has retained an exit-policy option, and CDIA is not on the high-concentration list as of 22 October 2026 [S8, S7, S12]. Status, not absolution.

Capital allocation became more shareholder-friendly and more leveraged at once. The FY2025 dividend was raised to US$50.0m from US$20.0m - about two fifths of FY2025 parent profit - and paid in 2026 while operating cash flow was negative [S17, S4]. The company also bought back 79.5m shares for US$4.6m without a general meeting, which reduces the float it is being asked to raise [S17, S8].

Related-party gravity is the central governance question. Related-party sales were 23.2% of nine-month revenue, with CAP the only customer above a tenth at US$12.8m [S17]. On the asset side sit the parent-issued equity-linked bonds of US$326.4m at a 6.8% coupon with an embedded 51.0% option over CAP's terminal and storage subsidiary, the US$245.2m loan to unlisted CAP subsidiaries at a 12.0% coupon, and US$230.3m of quoted shares whose issuers are not named [S17, S4, S2]. We carry the loan at face, the same basis as the filing; the earlier haircut was not sourced [S2]. These are disclosed and fair-valued, so optics-class rather than manipulation-class, but balance-sheet quality depends on the parent.
The auditor is Liana Ramon Xenia & Rekan, which issued an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 statements [S5]. There is no going-concern or late-filing notation [S17].

ESG exposures sit in the energy pillar - gas-fired generation, emissions and process safety - in the estate's water operations, and in the logistics fleet, where the group highlights solar capacity additions as its decarbonisation lever [S5].

The regime calendar dominates: the March 2027 free-float step, the April 2027 end of the MSCI consultation feedback and the June 2027 decision [S8, S11]. The FY2026 audited results and the dividend decision fall in the same window, and the port and storage projects target commercial operation in 2027 [S14]. The key operating test is whether capex keeps falling toward the depreciation rate now that the fleet build-out is largely done; a full year near our 85.0% assumption would be the first evidence that free cash flow can turn [S17].

Between updates the KPIs are revenue growth and segment mix, EBITDA on our operating definition, the fair-value and foreign-exchange lines, net debt and interest cover, the free float, the related-party revenue share, the AMP funding, and any change in the controller's stake [S17, S4, S8].

bear.narrative: Logistics charter rates soften after the fleet expansion, revenue growth halves and the energy segment's PLN pass-through margin compresses, while capex stays high, leverage keeps rising and the group has to fund the AMP balance and the 2031 maturity with dearer bank debt or a deeply discounted rights issue; the operating shocks below carry the earnings hit and the funding path is tested in section 5.

bull.narrative: The fleet and tank assets are integrated faster than planned, charter utilisation holds, energy volumes grow with the Krakatau industrial estate and capex normalises sooner; the group also meets the free-float step without a discounted sale and MSCI keeps Indonesia in the Emerging index, so index flows return to a still-thin float.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

adjustments.why: free float 9.77% must reach 12.5% by 2027-03-31 — controller sell-down or new shares inside the window [konglo deck S2]

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is anchored on the nine months (+16.4% year on year, S17), where logistics (time charter up 62%) carried the growth and electricity fell 1.6%; growth then fades as the acquired fleet annualises, to 12%, 10%, 9% and 8% before a 5% long-run rate. No volume decline is assumed.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Recalibrated on the nine months: the post-depreciation gross margin was 21.0% (S17, F55), not the 23.5% we carried, because the depreciation ratio stepped up from 6.5% of revenue in FY2025 to 12.2% while the ex-depreciation margin only rose from 30.4% to 33.2%. Holding the FY2025 post-depreciation margin through a five-point depreciation step implicitly assumed a five-point ex-depreciation expansion that the filing does not show. We use 22.0% for FY2026E (the fourth quarter carries the seasonal high, 26.3% post-depreciation in FY2025) rising to 23.5% as the fleet annualises.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 selling plus G&A was 8.8% of revenue (S4); the nine months of FY2026 ran at 11.8% (S17) but carried 6.9m of professional fees (S2) that we treat as non-recurring, so the underlying rate is about 6%. We keep 10.0% easing to 9.5%: above both the FY2025 level and the underlying run-rate, to allow for a listed-company cost base and the newly consolidated subsidiaries.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the filing: FY2025 depreciation was 9.62m (S4, F1) and the nine months of FY2026 alone 14.92m (S17, F56), 12.2% of nine-month revenue, as the acquired vessels entered service; we model 11.5% of revenue, slightly below the current run-rate because the fourth quarter adds revenue faster than it adds depreciation.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was 206m, or 139% of revenue, mostly the logistics fleet and tank additions (S4, F11). The nine months of FY2026 spent 121.3m, 99% of nine-month revenue, but the quarterly pace slowed to 27m in the third quarter (121.3m against 94.2m in the first half, S17, S9) and the fourth quarter of FY2025 carried only about half its revenue in capex; we therefore model 85% for FY2026E rather than the 105% we had. It then fades to a steady reinvestment rate: replacement at the D&A rate of 11.5% of revenue plus growth capex of about 2pp for the 2% terminal growth, so the long-run rate is 13.5% rather than replacement-only.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was 4.7% of revenue and 1.2% at 30 June 2026 (S4, S2); held at 5% of revenue.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate on operating profit
assumptions.basis: Operating EBIT is taxed at the 22% statutory rate the engine also uses in the WACC. The FY2025 3.2% group effective rate is an artefact of FVTPL gains, bond income taxed at source and equity-accounted associate income, none of which sit in operating EBIT (S4). H1 2026 tax was 8.31m on profit before tax of 27.63m, a 30% effective rate (S2), so 22% is not a cautious choice.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest expense on bank loans and leases was 28.25m on debt of 562.6m (S4), and the first half of FY2026 ran at 22.4m; we use 7.0%, consistent with the marginal bank pricing in Note 17.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance income was 24.3m, including 8.6m of bond coupons and 12.4m of deposit and current account interest (S4); on the reported cash balance that is about 4-5%, which we hold.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Restated to the nine months: debt rose from 562.6m at December 2025 to 894.3m at 30 September 2026 (S17, F81), a 331.7m increase, funded by 381.3m of new long-term bank loans while operating cash flow was negative. FY2026E therefore adds that actual increase; we then assume 100m in FY2027 and 50m in FY2028, then no net new debt.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Recurring non-operating income is the coupon and fair-value income on the 553m bond portfolio and the 12.4m share of associate profit (S4); the 74.1m FVTPL gain in FY2025 is not repeated. We carry 30m a year, falling to 25m in perpetuity as bonds mature.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities took 6.74m of FY2025 net profit of 127.79m, or 5.3% (S4); held at 5.5%.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 dividend was raised to 50.0m and paid in 2026 (50.0m of cash dividends in the nine months, S17, F92) against FY2025 parent profit of 121.1m (S4), a 41% payout; the FY2024 distribution was 20.0m. We model a 40% payout of current-year parent earnings: the last actual ratio, and a distribution the group has chosen to fund with debt while capex is heavy.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No share issuance is assumed in the base: the free-float rule and the registry float are sourced (S8, S10), but the company has not announced whether its remedy will be a controller sell-down, a placement or a rights issue. We treat the placement/rights route as a dilution risk in section 5 rather than a base input, and the IPO shares are already in the share count (S4).

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The house long-run setting for an Indonesian infrastructure operator - long-run nominal GDP growth, below the five-year forecast path; it is a house parameter, not a company disclosure. The statements are in US dollars and most revenue is dollar-linked, so the model runs in the reporting currency and the terminal rate is set against Indonesian nominal growth rather than US inflation.

challenges.challenge: The price that sets both the expected return and the konglo premium ratio is 436, an intraday datapack print of 2026-10-27 09:41, but the archived registry the report itself cites (S10) shows the 27 October close at 398 and the 28 October close at 386. The report is dated 30 October, after the 29 October results. At 386 the premium ratio falls from 4.64x to about 4.11x and the lens target from 313 to about 284, so the stated -27.9% is wrong in either direction (about -26% at 386 on a recomputed target, or -18.9% if only the price is fixed).
challenges.answer: The challenge is right. The 436 figure was an intraday datapack print (27 October 09:41). I refreshed the pack through fund record pack, which now carries the 29 October close of 362 (price_date 2026-10-29), and disclosed the price date at the top of the report and in section 4. On 362 the lens premium ratio is 3.03x, the target is 287 and the expected total return is -20.5%, so the rating moves to REDUCE; the prior -27.9% was an artefact of the stale print. The table of record shows 386 on 28 October and 398 the day before, consistent with the refreshed series.

challenges.challenge: Interest cover and AFFO are flagged in one line but the scenario set has no leverage channel. Nine-month finance costs of 40.2m (F59) exceed operating EBIT of about 11.2m; OCF is -6.3m (F91), AFFO is negative and net debt is about 408m at 30 September (894.3m debt, F81) - roughly 10x EBITDA - while 50m of dividends and a 4.6m buyback were funded with new debt. S2 Note 16 shows a 272.2m principal maturity in 2031 and 166.7m in 2032, and the Rp4tn term loan carries a Total Interest-Bearing Debt/Equity covenant of 3x (S2 p.68). The bear only cuts revenue growth by 4pp and gross margin by 2pp; it does not test refinancing, covenant or equity-raise paths.
challenges.answer: Accepted and built. Section 5 now carries a dedicated leverage-and-refinancing risk paragraph: nine-month finance costs of US$40.2m against an operating result of gross profit less selling and administrative costs, FY2025 finance costs of US$28.9m against EBIT of US$22.3m, operating cash flow of -US$6.3m against +US$7.7m a year earlier, and the repayment calendar (US$272.2m in 2031, US$166.7m in 2032, US$103.0m in 2035 against US$772.6m of principal). The 3x Total IBD/Equity covenant is disclosed but the actual ratio is far inside it (debt of US$894.3m against equity of US$1,111.5m), so I rebut the implied near-term covenant breach and locate the risk in liquidity and the funding path: the AMP balance and negative OCF are drawn from the same bank lines, and the remedies are portfolio asset sales or a rights issue. The rights-issue path is analysed: struck at today's premium it lifts fundamental value per share but compresses the konglo premium, so dilution is a premium risk, not a DCF risk. The bear narrative now carries the funding stress and states that no covenant breach is modelled because the headroom does not support one.

challenges.challenge: The 9M filing (S17 Note 10, p.66) and S14 disclose a US$90m subscription for 40% of PT Armada Maritim Persada signed on 30 June 2026; only US$30.95m is carried as an associate at 30 September, leaving about US$60m unfunded. The report mentions neither the deal nor the commitment, and the post-balance-sheet review concludes no material events were found. A US$60m commitment is around 10% of bridge equity and further strains a company with negative operating cash flow.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The AMP transaction is now disclosed in sections 1, 3 and 5, and in the post-balance-sheet review: the US$90.0m conditional subscription for 40% of PT Armada Maritim Persada signed on 30 June 2026, US$30.0m paid in the nine months and US$30.95m carried as an associate at 30 September, so the balance is unfunded. The report states that the commitment is not in the DCF cash flows and not a bridge liability, because it is a purchase instalment that converts into an asset at cost; it is a cash call funded from the same bank lines as the capex, and the funding path is now a named risk. Facts F114, F115, F116 and F126 are registered with verbatim quotes.

challenges.challenge: Associates are carried at book (172.8m at 30 June) with no test of value. The 45% KPE stake was acquired for US$200m (S5, F40) but is carried at US$79.3m (F44, S2) - a 60% gap - and the group also holds the KTI water associate and, through the ELB, an option on 51% of a CAP terminal business. The report gives no reason for the write-down and no recovery case, so the bridge may understate the assets and the single largest non-operating holding is untested.
challenges.answer: Accepted in part, with a sourced correction to the framing. The KPE carrying-value gap is now explained and tested in section 4. The US$200m annual-report line is a milestone description of the stake's worth at acquisition, not a carrying value; the equity-accounted book reflects KPE's equity after project debt, and the 2023 top-up of the remaining stake cost US$46.4m for 35 percentage points (F117), which corroborates a much lower equity value than the US$200m enterprise worth. It was therefore not a 60% write-down. The recovery test is earnings-based: KPE contributed US$2.39m of associate profit in the first half with no impairment indicator, so book is the most likely mark and a recovery belongs in the bull narrative, not the base. The ELB's 51% option over the CAP terminal and storage subsidiary is now disclosed (S2 Note 12) and explained as embedded in the fair-value mark, and the port and storage projects are stated to be inside the forecast cash flows.

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA cross-check applies 15.85x to the data pack's LTM EBITDA of 17.1m, which the report itself calls a depreciation-error figure, and then cuts the method to 10% weight. On the filing's corrected LTM EBITDA (about 35-40m) the same multiple gives roughly Rp160-165 a share, not 114, so the reported cross-check does not test the DCF. The house POWER_UTILITIES weights are 60/30/10; a 90/10 split is a large deviation and the dividend-yield method is dropped without comment.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The cross-check now runs on the filing's EBITDA rather than the data pack's depreciation-error LTM: I restated FY2025A and FY2024A revenue from the audited statements (F106, F107), which makes the engine rebuild LTM from the filing, and the metric is US$31.9m instead of US$17.1m. At the peer median the cross-check is now Rp155 a share, 67.5% above the DCF, and the report states it. The four names with an EV/EBITDA in the peer table are BREN, KEEN, PGEO and POWR; the 15.9x median is the mean of the two middle names (KEEN and PGEO) and is reproducible from the pack's peer table, while BREN is the highest and carries no weight in a median. I restored the house POWER_UTILITIES weights 60/30/10, including the dividend-yield check that the prior version dropped without comment (it values the shares at Rp138 on the peer median yield), and the QC weights.changed flag no longer fires.

challenges.challenge: The related-party loan (238.0m) is carried at 80% of face - a 47.6m haircut - with no source for the 20%, while the larger 326.4m CAP-linked ELB and the 206.8m FVTPL quoted shares are carried at 100% even though the report says balance-sheet quality depends on the parent's credit. S2 Note 13 also shows the ELB is tied to an option to subscribe 51% of a CAP terminal/storage subsidiary; the report describes it only as a bond.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The 20% haircut on the related-party loan had no source and has been removed: the loan is carried at face, the same basis as the filing, supported by a 12% fixed coupon and no impairment or expected-credit-loss provision in Note 30 (F124). The credit basis is now consistent across the three assets: the loan at face, the equity-linked bonds at their fair-value mark, and the quoted shares at Level-1 fair value. Section 6 discloses that the ELB carries an option to subscribe 51% of CAP's terminal and storage subsidiary (F119), with the exercise window extended to July 2054, and that it is not exercised as of 30 June 2026.

challenges.challenge: The frontmatter summary and thesis say profit fell because last year's fair-value gains did not repeat, but F61 shows income from financial assets was US$16.83m in both 9M2025 and 9M2026 - flat. The decline is the other-gains line (45.4m to 3.5m), the one-off land/other gain, plus finance costs (21.0m to 40.2m). Section 3 gets the attribution right; the summary and thesis contradict the body and the filing.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The summary and thesis now attribute the profit decline to the non-recurring other gain (US$45.4m in 9M2025 against US$3.5m in 9M2026) and higher finance costs (US$40.2m), and state explicitly that financial-asset income was flat at US$16.83m in both periods. The body already had the attribution right; the summary and thesis no longer contradict it, and all three now cite F64, F59 and F61.

challenges.challenge: The cost of capital is cited to [S2], which contains no risk-free rate, ERP, CRP or beta. The model metadata shows an industry-default unlevered beta of 0.60 (levered 0.72), while S10 reports a one-year beta of 1.99. The D/E of 0.256 is 30 June gross debt of 768.0m over a market cap of about US$3.0bn, so it uses the premium-inflated price the report calls 4.6x value - a circularity in the discount rate. A higher beta or a fundamental-weighted gearing changes the DCF materially.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The cost-of-capital inputs are no longer cited to S2: the report now states they are a house build (risk-free rate, ERP, CRP and the house unlevered beta for power utilities) and cites the filing only for the cost of debt. The gearing convention is stated: gross debt over market capitalisation at the 29 October close, which is itself a premium to fundamental value, so the gearing and WACC are understated against a fundamental structure, a bias that flatters the DCF. The observed one-year beta of 1.99 (F120, S10) is disclosed and tested: I rebut its use as the anchor because it is a regression on a year in which the shares fell by four fifths with a thin float, and I state that at that beta the WACC would leave the sensitivity grid; the grid itself is in the report.

challenges.challenge: The bull regime target of 551 (premium widening 10%) is attributed to an asset injection or placement that would fix the float. A placement or controller sell-down increases supply and dilutes per-share value - it should compress the premium, not widen it - and the report gives no sourced channel by which the premium rises 26% above today's price. The genuine re-rating channels (index re-inclusion after compliance, the MSCI decision, an accretive group asset injection) are not argued.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bull regime target is no longer attributed to an asset injection or placement that fixes the float; the report now separates float repair (compression) from re-rating (index and flows): the bull channel is MSCI keeping Indonesia in the Emerging index at the June 2027 decision and lifting its freeze, so passive money returns to a float of 9.8% once the company meets the March steps, with an accretive asset injection at a fair price as the second channel. The base case keeps compression, consistent with the lens.

challenges.challenge: Section 1 says time charter more than doubled its nine-month revenue; F72 shows US$39.97m against US$24.67m, +62%, which the investment summary states correctly. More than doubled overstates the growth and is inconsistent within the report.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The 'more than doubled' phrase is gone; section 1 now states time charter revenue as US$40.0m in nine months against US$34.6m for all of FY2025, with the facts carrying the figures, and the summary and body are consistent.

challenges.challenge: Terminal growth of 2.0% is cited to [S4], the audited FY2025 filing, which states no terminal growth rate; the assumptions basis also calls the company rupiah-reporting and dollar-earning although the statements are in US dollars (S4, S17). The beta and terminal growth come from house config, not the filing.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Terminal growth is no longer cited to S4: the assumptions basis now states it is the house long-run setting for an Indonesian infrastructure operator, not a company disclosure, with S4 and S17 cited only for the currency. The currency description is corrected to US-dollar reporting and largely dollar-linked revenue.

challenges.challenge: The EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS card requires an accruals ratio and a cash-conversion trend. The report flags fair value, FX and related-party revenue but gives no accruals metric. Net income of 32.2m against operating cash flow of -6.3m on assets of about 1.9bn is roughly a 2% accruals ratio - not alarming, but it should be stated so the card is visibly run.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Section 3 now carries the accruals test: net profit against the operating cash outflow on average total assets (the 30 September balance and the prior year-end), a low single-digit ratio well inside the card's alarm level. The cash-conversion trend is stated: operating cash flow covered under a tenth of profit a year earlier and is negative now. The flags are classified: fair-value marks, FX and related-party revenue are optics-class; no manipulation-class flag and no board or notation issue was found.

missing_bull_case.note: Understates owned assets: the 45% KPE stake bought for US$200m (S5, F40) is carried at US$79.3m (F44, S2) with no explanation or recovery test; the 51% CAP terminal option inside the 326.4m ELB, the port/storage COD in 2027 and the new AMP mining-logistics stake are not valued. The bull regime target of 551 is also mis-attributed to a float fix that should compress the premium, not widen it.

missing_bear_case.note: No leverage or liquidity case despite the facts: 9M finance costs 40.2m (F59) exceed operating EBIT of about 11.2m, OCF is -6.3m (F91) and AFFO negative, debt is 894.3m (F81) (~10x EBITDA), with a 272.2m maturity in 2031, 166.7m in 2032 and a 3x debt/equity covenant (S2 Note 16). The US$60m unfunded AMP subscription is absent from the risks and the post-balance-sheet review.

assumption_realism.note: The capex cut from 105% to 85% of revenue is the sole driver of the 27% EV increase (60.2m to 76.3m) and the fundamental value rising from 97.5 to 101.7 between v1 and v4. It rests on one quarter's 27m Q3 pace against 99% of revenue spent in 9M, and the update never bridges v1 to v4. Most other inputs are sourced and conservative.

evidence_and_citations.note: Price 436 (datapack 27 Oct 09:41 intraday) contradicts S10's 27 Oct close of 398 and 28 Oct close of 386. "Fair-value gains did not repeat" contradicts F61 (16.83m in both periods). "More than doubled" is +62% (F72). The 15.85x peer median and "four-name peer set" are not reproducible from cov_publish comps, which shows two names.

valuation_method_fit.note: EV/EBITDA is applied to the data-pack LTM EBITDA of 17.1m that the report itself rejects as a depreciation error, then cut to 10% weight; on the filing's EBITDA the same multiple gives roughly Rp160-165, so the cross-check is not a test of the DCF. Cost-of-capital inputs are cited to S2, which contains no rates or beta.

bias_and_tone.note: The summary and thesis overstate the earnings story (F61 fair-value income is flat, not a non-repeat) and the target moves only Rp2 despite materially worse 9M debt and cash flow. The SELL is not driven by a heroic input and the base value rise on lower capex is sourced; the bias is in the narrative and the stale price, not in the rating direction.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: No commodity or royalty deck applies to an estate utility; the macro inputs (USD_IDR, BI path) are read consistently, the coal deck is correctly absent, and the free-float and MSCI dates match the registry and S8/S11. The 12.5%/15% tiering is correctly applied to a >Rp5tn cap.

conservatism_audit.note: Unjustified conservatism: the 238.0m related-party loan is marked at 80% of face (a 47.6m haircut) with no source. Unjustified optimism: the larger 326.4m CAP-linked ELB and the 206.8m FVTPL quoted shares are carried at 100%, though the report says quality depends on the parent's credit. The ELB is an option to buy 51% of a CAP subsidiary (S2 Note 13), not a plain bond. Opex 10% and gross margin 22% are above/below actuals with sources.

calibration.note: qc reports no BLOCK flags. The FY2025A margin gap of 1.93pp is explained by the D&A add-back rising from 6.5% to 11.5% of revenue and by Q4 seasonality (2025 Q4 gross margin 26.3%), both sourced; the capex drift and konglo overlay WARN flags are justified.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. Read the packet, the rendered report, fund record and all 12 red-team challenges; re-ran draft lint (PASS) and comps --industry POWER_UTILITIES. Base is the most likely path: the calibration gate is exact on FY2025A (EBITDA 31.92 = gross profit 35.39 less SG&A 13.09 plus D&A 9.62, S4) and FY2026E is anchored on the 9M actual (revenue +16.4%, post-D&A gross margin 21.0%, Q4 seasonality 26.3% from FY2025), with mirrored business scenarios (+/-4pp growth, +/-2pp margin) at 25/50/25 and the capex drift answered at the gate with S17/S9/F90. The mild P&L conservatism (opex 10% vs 8.8% FY2025; cost of debt 7.0% vs 5.0-5.8% paid) is offset by the FY2026 capex normalisation to 85% of revenue; QC and judge both neutral, and neither moves the rating. Konglo lens applied on fundamentals, not toward the price: the fundamental is built first (method blend Rp116 today, probability-weighted 12-month value Rp130, today's value Rp119.5) and the overlay is deterministic from the deck (compress base 0.30 + ff_deadline 0.05 = 0.35 closing share; bear 0.75, bull -0.10), giving target Rp287 = 130 x 2.203 with the price at 3.03x today's value. The reviewed price is the 29 October close of 362 (pack price_date 2026-10-29) and the published snapshot is frozen under history/v1 (price 436, SELL Rp311) - evidence and freeze law hold. TR -20.5% is REDUCE under fund rules (SELL <= -25), so SELL to REDUCE is the band outcome of a price that fell more than the target, not a change of view. No consensus contamination: the sources are the FY2025 audited LK, the H1/9M LK, the annual report, IDX/OJK/MSCI and company press, with no broker material and consensus sentences removed at fetch; the EV/EBITDA peer median of 15.85x is set by KEEN (20.2x) and PGEO (11.5x), so BREN's 36.6x konglo premium does not enter CDIA's cross-check. Batch bias: CDIA is the only name at signoff (BREN is parked); the industry is not uniformly tilted by a shared input - both Barito names screen below the price because their premiums are extreme (BREN 10.8x, CDIA 3.03x) and the fundamental methods are independent of the regime overlay. Carried QC NOTEs Q1-Q4 are non-blocking and disclosed: Q1 bridge stays at 30 June; Q2 FY2026E parent profit 23.87 is below the 9M actual 30.26 without a Q4 bridge; Q3 the Level-1 label on the 206.8m quoted shares; Q4 one-period accruals. Two group/desk items for the Director, not grounds for a return: (1) TPIA's published SOTP marks the 40% CDIA minority at the prior CDIA house fundamental (today's value about Rp89.6/share), which this revision lifts to about Rp119.5, so TPIA's mark is now stale by roughly US$60-80m - TPIA is the file to refresh, and it marks at house value rather than market, so the konglo group rule is met on method; (2) the 206.8m quoted shares are carried at market and the issuers are unnamed, so if a later filing identifies covered Barito siblings the premium should be stripped from the bridge. At the next version, disclose the FY2026E Q4 revenue build (+25% q/q in the model against +14% in FY2025 Q4) and put the negative AFFO against the 10y FR yield numerically, which the INFRA card requires and the report currently states only qualitatively. Approved; left at signoff for the Director to publish.

bias.note: Base is anchored on the 9M actual (revenue +16.4%, post-D&A gross margin 21.0%, Q4 seasonality sourced at 26.3%); mild P&L conservatism (opex 10% vs 8.8% FY2025, cost of debt 7.0% vs 5.0-5.8% paid) is offset by mildly optimistic capex (85% vs 99% of 9M revenue) and 22% tax vs 30% H1 effective; scenarios are mirrored (+/-4pp growth, +/-2pp margin) at 25/50/25 and the target is set by the konglo lens, so no drift moves the rating.

recomputed.item: Net debt at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3 movement disclosed)

findings.finding: Bridge stays at 30 June (net debt 347.7) against 30 Sep 408.35; the post_bs_review quantifies the Q3 movements (+23.5 shares, +7.2 loan, +32.3 associates, +60.7 net debt) and they net to +2.2m, 0.35% of bridge equity - verified below the 1% claim and immaterial; judge concurs.

FY2026E parent profit of 23.87m is below the 9M actual of 30.26m, implying a Q4 loss from higher finance costs and D&A with no one-off gains; the report does not bridge Q4. No target impact (DCF is FCFF-driven and DPS is 10% weight).

The 206.8m quoted-share bridge item is labelled 'Level-1 quoted listed shares'; S2 Note 7 says only 'investment in shares classified as financial assets at FVTPL' and does not state the fair-value level in the text.
EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS asks for a three-year accruals ratio; the report gives one period (9M2026 vs FY2025 average assets) with inputs stated, which answers red-team C12 but not the three-year trend.

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 3.03x fundamental value (premium); the base case closes 35% of the log gap in 12 months (ff_deadline); target 287 vs fundamental 12-month value 130 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The konglo lens is applied to a built fundamental: the price is a premium to today's fundamental value because the registry free float is 9.77% against the 12.5% step due 31 March 2027 [S10, S8], so the ff_deadline overlay adds 0.05 to the closing share and the base regime case closes 35% of the log gap; the lens is explained in sections 4 and 5 and the profile table sits in section 6.
